en: They would not lower his crown-beam,
They hung his head in the garden of paradise.
Any man who went straight against them,
Was commanded in this way.
In the middle of its broad enclosure,
All around was a plane-tree garden.
Look upon the raging scourge’s game.
See the map of every devil within him,
His executioners numbered seven companies,
Six accusers made six companies,
And within them he alone,
Placed a guard at Bitashka,
Saying a sovereign had risen in his place,
They named him Chyngteñir.
He had champions and brave men,
He had strength that reached across the world.
The sovereign is not God,
Yet his command was like God Most High’s,
Nowhere was he destitute.
At first, watching day and night,
His frenzy rose and seized him,
His envoys to right and left,
He drove toward the Kyrgyz people.
Taking word from his envoy,
Of the accuser stricken by darkness,
A wolf that drank blood.
Ruining all of his people,
He sent forth his massed thousands.
He was poison, and he was blood,
He was a soul of bitter wrath.
His majesty was fearsome and his strength great,
Taking the whole world in his hand,
He was one who said, “I know.”
Crushing all who encountered him,
Gnawing all who crossed his path,
Setting his face toward the whole world,
He circled in a boiling rage,
He lashed out like a boar,
Burning with his wrath.
Chyng Tengir grew wrathful,
Calling upon the blue-gray hero,
Raging like a blue-gray boar,
His splendid form appeared like iron,
His eyes and heart were set apart,
He readied his tens of thousands,
He prepared his champions,
His warrior aspect appeared,
Forty-fold calamity made them tremble,
He moved and thundered,
Trembling without letting the day pass,
He issued a sweeping command.
When they came to the tower,
The tower of hell,
Do not ask of that tower,
Nine thousand fathoms high,
A war drum crafted by a master,
When they beat the war drum,
It split heads beneath the hellish sun,
Its striking could be heard afar.
The war drum stood firm,
Do not ask about the war drum’s voice.
It was the signal that the enemy had come,
The lamb cries out in hunger,
The wrathful thousand stood grim,
All the brave men who stood there,
The gathered lions,
Without moving or making a twitch,
A fiercely wrathful fire engulfed them,
Even under pressure they would not stir,
When he lunged at the stone-hearted,
He had no desire for the sand-hearted,
How many enduring ones were among them,
When he attacked, he spared no life,
He drove them on as a champion.
His mind unsated, he steeled his face,
All who faced him,
Death struck amid the uproar,
The people scattered and the land was ruined,
When grievous calamity remained,
The remaining people took up the whip,
Gathering what was done in an instant,
Saying, “Seek life beneath the moon,”
Sending each to his own place,
He brought measureless devastation.
From a thousand men, a hundred souls,
He selected and took them.
Saying that the khan’s command remained,
The sand caught fire and stone burned,
He set down a scorched cauldron.
Making the strongest suffer,
Making the last ones wail,
Making sparks fly from mottled eyes,
From mottled eyes into wind and fire,
Once enraged, he never retreated,
Destroying whoever confronted him,
In the task he faced head-on,
He did not return before dying,
From those assembled, he selected and took them.
Chyngteñir gathered an army,
He set forth what God had ordained.
Coming into sight before the Kyrgyz,
He acted harshly toward many,
Thinking, “My strength will suffice,”
Against the eighteen thousand worlds.
Turning him against a thousand men,
He launched a fine army.
One soul for every hundred men,
Was left in another army.
An uproar arose that split the earth,
A din arose that rent the sky,
Preparing the bellows and preparing the work,
The broad enclosure filled up.
The eighteen thousand worlds,
Heaped upon the Kyrgyz,
Its extent filled up like a mountain.
Ten thousand against a single man,
All of them gathered here.
A multitude that shook the earth,
Waving hands and mustering the army,
Driving his forces against the enemy,
Chyngteñir’s black banner,
A vast uproar that shattered the sky,
Beast-like, filthy and grim,
It came in surging masses,
Raging and growing venomous,
The black earth beneath the multitude,
Stopped under the violent force.
Warring against the whole world,
Laying the world waste,
This earth did not collapse,
Under his withering wrath,
It halted beneath the multitude.
There were champions and majesty,
There were countless kinds of multitudes.
The coursing pursuers,
A calamity that greased the earth,
A great host filled every ravine.
The land where his army spread,
The clans became an army of tens of thousands,
The earth stirred beneath the mist,
Taking an engulfing army of tens of thousands,
Arrayed like blue-gray iron,
The defenders despaired of life,
Ruining the land and shaking the people,
His black wrath became known,
Every person with understanding,
Despaired even of their own lives,
The worm had entered the snare,
Unable to understand after losing his senses,
It became a stain spread like water,
The people multiplied and raised an uproar,
The worm had entered the snare.
A torment unknown to humankind,
Had plunged into the uproar,
Whispering became a great rumor,
Had entered the snare.
Of this ill-fated black multitude,
None had the freedom to speak openly.
Speaking only in whispers,
Taking up the blue standard,
Raising an uproar across the face of the earth,
At the time pride swelled in his breast,
Ruining the people and slaughtering the land,
Starting strife throughout the whole world,
Breaking into the innermost place of hell,
At the time when he would do so,
He punished whoever crossed his path,
He exacted vengeance from whoever opposed him,
At the time when he dealt it out.
One faction into the world,
Saying it was time to set it at the head,
Everything gathered and collected,
Children, family, livestock, and property,
Without seeing daylight, toward the rear,
Saying, “We are going to leave them behind,”
Against the guiltless Kalmyks,
The Kyrgyz in strength of arms,
Saying, “We are going to lead them,”
Seven generations would neither see it nor shoot an arrow,
We were to enter the fight and prevail,
Against a guiltless world,
We were to attack and prevail.
The punishment of those who were caught,
It seems we were going to administer it,
Meeting one another face to face,
We were destined to die in victory,
Many among the people have grown beards,
Many people wander pale and wasted,
Many people go about unable to walk,
Many are blind and know not what to do,
Growing bearded and turning pale,
Stricken with jaundice and left astonished,
Chyng Tengir was the sovereign,
His heroism became known,
Making all the people wait,
The people did not tend their freely grazing sheep,
Saying, “God will strike the fool,”
Going on this way among the Kalmyks,
Saying promises would leave them exhausted,
Saying a ravaged people would be formed,
To scatter the whole world,
To flee from one pasture to another,
What was said early became late,
His two eyes became four with anxious watching,
Many people went away and wandered,
Before Chyngteñir’s venomous wrath,
Unable to escape, despairing of life,
Many people fell sick and wan.
With neither rope nor cord,
His eyes were bound toward the grave,
In the blood of the Kalday heart,
He drove everyone from the multitude,
One soul for a host of men,
The khan had them put on display.
Mounted on a pale horse like a mountain,
Wearing a coat that roared like a forest,
A mace like a mountain was strapped on,
With the champion’s hellish venom,
Circling layer upon layer,
His hand-sized eyes showed,
Wearing a deep-blue iron coat,
Behold the champion Chyngteñir,
Behind the host, a blazing glacier,
In his leathered hand, a fiery blade,
Binding his people together into one,
Tengir became khan in the capital,
Army upon army gathered,
His impetuous hour was coming,
The mind reels and words cannot reach it,
It burned the breast like an ember,
A fiery mass came from the stone.
You are like an enemy who slaughters men,
The devil’s hour was coming,
The Chinese host that wished to see no sun,
Its hour to overrun the land was coming.
Such was the place that had been dug.
The people and their allies were hard pressed,
The affairs of men were ruined.
How immense was this fiery majesty,
Where could the afflicted soul find refuge?
Across ridge after ridge and many deserts,
They came marching onward,
Like a river flowing through a valley,
They came surging onward,
Making a wondrous uproar,
Raising tumult across the empty steppe,
The wind swept past the watching ibex,
The wind thundered where the kulan ran,
They came onward in splendor,
Advancing in confusion from many sides,
The great army that came from the Shibe,
Its afflicted commander of a thousand,
Drove them onward,
At the place where they halted,
That warrior Chyng Tengir,
Into the tent before him,
